hypothesis: A density-dependent chemical-spread direction can retain a nonzero adjacency signature while a smooth analytical density correction limits its scan-transmittance excursion.

research_basis.source: Ehn and Silevitch, Diffusion model for the adjacency effect in viscous development, JOSA 64(5), 1974
research_basis.use: mechanism precedent for density-dependent chemical spread; not parameter calibration

research_basis.source: Rajkowski and Nowak, Numerical investigation of sharpness in photographic layers containing DIR compounds, 1999
research_basis.use: mechanism precedent for exposure scatter plus chemical spread; not parameter calibration

forbidden_fallbacks: change any P5B chart, threshold or visual veto
fit the candidate bound after viewing confirmatory results
hard clip density, transmittance or scan-linear values
move the correction out of developed-density domain
call generic bounds measured film, process or stock parameters

branch_rule.pass: retain the bounded adjacency candidate for combined synthetic OOD and full-image evaluation
branch_rule.fail: close bounded adjacency and use zero-adjacency while retaining forward scatter, dye diffusion and scanner MTF
